correctness.rationale: The geometry is reconstructed from the maximal-orthogonal-Grassmannian Schubert basis and one-box Pieri rule: the top power of the minimal Picard generator counts saturated chains to the staircase strict partition. The shifted hook-length product gives the displayed factorial quotient. Applying Legendre valuation and the identity \(s_2(2a-1)=s_2(a-1)+1\) cancels every non-binary term and yields exactly \(n-s_2(n(n+1)/2)\). The small residue cases are checked directly and the bound for \(n\ge7\) proves the complete modulo-four classification.

value.rationale: The minimally embedded spinor varieties form a canonical homogeneous family, and their projective degrees are basic enumerative invariants. The theorem gives the exact power of two in every complementary linear-section count by a closed binary statistic, rather than isolated values. It also produces complete oddness and modulo-four classifications, including the exceptional dimensions corresponding to degrees \(2\) and \(286\). This is a natural arithmetic invariant of a standard algebraic-geometric family and is not a chosen numerical slice.
